results.summary_before: This project implements a 16-byte RAM built from D flip-flops. It supports read and write operations with a 4-bit address, active-low chip enable and load signals, and an 8-bit data input. The design is intended for integration into an 8-bit processor and includes CocoTB testbenches that verify write and read functionality across all addresses.

results.summary_before: This design computes a running longitudinal redundancy check (LRC) over a stream of bytes, updating the code each time a new byte is presented on the input pins. A byte is supplied on ui_in and the current LRC is read from uo_out, with the running value resetting when the chip is reset. No external hardware is needed, and the design is a straightforward combinational/sequential checksum generator. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand the function and basic usage.

results.summary_before: This project implements a basic leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron in SystemVerilog. It integrates input current by addition and leaks by dividing by two at each time step, with an enable pin advancing time roughly once per second when clocked at about 50 MHz. The neuron fires a spike when the integrated value exceeds a threshold, and it includes a timeout to prevent constant output from overstimulation. Testing involves manually setting input switches to provide current and observing spike output on LEDs, with a dedicated LED indicating time steps.
